transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

# What 22E Means

On Samsung side-by-side fridges like the RS68A8820S9, 22E (sometimes shown as 22C) is a fridge fan error. The control board has detected that the fan circulating cold air in the fridge compartment isn't spinning properly. That explains why the fridge side is warm while the freezer may still be fine.

## Most Common Cause: Ice Build-Up

In most cases the fan motor isn't broken. It's blocked by ice forming around the fridge evaporator behind the rear panel. This usually happens because of:
• A door left slightly open or not sealing properly
• A worn or dirty door gasket letting in humid air
• Frequent or long door openings
• A defrost system problem (heater, sensor, or drain), which is less common but more serious

## Fixes You Can Try

1. Full manual defrost (most effective)
• Move food to a cool box or another fridge.
• Unplug the fridge (or switch it off at the wall).
• Leave the doors open for at least 8–12 hours, ideally 24. Put towels down for meltwater.
• Plug it back in and give it several hours to reach temperature (a full day to fully stabilise).

2. Forced defrost mode (quicker, if available)
Many Samsung models have a hidden service mode, usually entered by pressing and holding two buttons together (often Fridge + Freezer or similar) for about 8–10 seconds until the display goes blank or changes, then cycling to the defrost setting ("Fd"). The exact combination varies by model, so check your manual or Samsung's support page for the RS68A before trying it. If you're unsure, the unplugging method is just as effective, only slower.

3. Reset the error
Unplugging for 5–10 minutes can clear the code. This won't fix an underlying ice problem, though, so the error will likely return.

4. Check the doors and seals
• Make sure the door closes fully on its own and isn't obstructed by items inside.
• Clean the gaskets with warm soapy water and check for tears or gaps. A paper slip closed in the door should hold with some resistance all the way around.
• Check that the fridge is level and tilted slightly back so the doors swing shut.

5. Don't block the air vents inside the fridge compartment.

## When to Call for Repair

Contact Samsung or a technician if:
• The error comes back within days or weeks after a full defrost. This points to a faulty defrost heater, defrost sensor, or blocked drain.
• You hear no fan noise at all even after defrosting, which suggests a failed fan motor.
• The fan is noisy or grinding.

The appliance is from 2021 onward, so check your warranty status. Samsung's standard warranty in the EU/UK is typically 2 years on parts, with longer cover (often 10–20 years) on the Digital Inverter compressor only, which wouldn't cover a fan or defrost fault. Some retailers or extended warranties may cover it, though.

## Food Safety

While the fridge side is warm, check the temperature if you can. Food held above 8°C for more than a few hours (especially meat, dairy, and leftovers) should be discarded.

In the majority of cases, a thorough defrost plus fixing any door-seal issue clears 22E for good.

The fridge side reads 9C at the moment. There's no burning smell and nothing has tripped. I tried switching it off at the wall for a few minutes but the code came back within a few hours. Should I go ahead with the full defrost?

# Yes, go ahead with the full defrost

A few minutes off clears the error but doesn't melt any ice, so the code returning within hours is expected and still points to an iced-up fan.

## Deal with the food first

9°C is too warm. A fridge should be at 5°C or below. Food that has been above 8°C for more than about four hours, especially milk, meat, fish, cooked leftovers and soft cheese, is best thrown away. Move anything still safe to a cool box with ice packs, or to the freezer side if it's still cold.

## Doing the defrost

• Unplug it rather than just turning the temperature down. The freezer side will thaw too, so empty it as well.
• Leave both doors open for a full 24 hours if you can. Ice behind the rear panel melts slowly, and stopping early is the most common reason the error comes straight back.
• Put towels on the floor and in the bottom of the compartments for the meltwater.
• Speed it up safely with bowls of hot water placed inside and the doors closed for 20–30 minutes at a time, or a room fan blowing into the compartments.
• Avoid sharp tools for chipping ice, and avoid heat guns or hairdryers aimed close up. It's easy to puncture a refrigerant line or warp the plastic.
• Check the seals while it's empty. Clean the gaskets with warm soapy water and look for tears. You can also close a sheet of paper in the door at several points around the seal. It should resist when you pull it out. If it slides out freely anywhere, that gap may be letting in the moist air that caused the ice.

## After restarting

Give it several hours before restocking, and up to a day to fully settle. Then watch what happens:

| What happens | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| No code, fridge reaches 3–5°C and stays there | Fixed. It was ice, probably from a door or seal issue |
| Code returns within hours of restarting | The fan motor itself is probably faulty |
| Code returns after days or weeks | Ice is building up again: a defrost heater, sensor, or drain fault, or a bad seal |

If the code comes back in either of the last two cases, book a Samsung engineer or a qualified repairer rather than defrosting repeatedly. Check your warranty status first, as a fan or defrost fault may be covered depending on the fridge's age.
